about: Declarative rejection corpus. Each case applies its RFC 6902 patch list to a deep copy
of the named base fixture at test collection time, then asserts that the validator
reports EXACTLY the rule ids in `expect` - no more, no fewer. Do not hand-write broken
JSON files: they rot the moment a schema changes (docs/worked-example.md section 6).
Started from the 28 cases in worked-example.md section 6, extended per ruling R-14 to
cover every BP-* and DS-* rule in docs/contracts.md section 3.
`expect: []`      the mutation must validate CLEAN - used to pin a deliberate skip
`resolver`        which corpus resolver stub to use; default knows the golden
blueprint as published for datasets and nothing for blueprints
`parse_raises`    the mutated document does not parse as its Pydantic model, by
design (ruling R-23's strict numerics). The rule still fires,
because the validator runs against the raw dict
`note`            why the case is shaped the way it is

cases.note: Ruling R-14 replaced the shipped case, which renamed nodes/2 and thereby orphaned every edge that referenced it - firing BP-004 and BP-005 as well. Appending a second node with an existing id duplicates the id without touching an edge.

value.notes: A second node claiming the id `complete`.

cases.note: An added edge rather than a retargeted one: retargeting `to` would orphan the old target and fire BP-005 too.

BP-005 is skipped when entry_node names no node - otherwise every node in the graph reports as unreachable on top of this one finding. This case covers BP-006's existence half only. The inbound-edge half cannot be isolated by ANY blueprint: an edge into entry_node forces either a cycle (BP-018) or a predecessor unreachable from the entry (BP-005), so an exact-set case is impossible. Ruling R-31 gives that half a rule-half exemption in the coverage gate, naming the membership-style unit test that covers it: see RULE_HALF_EXEMPTIONS in tests/unit/test_validation_drift.py.

0, never a non-integer: `max_iterations` is StrictInt on the model (ruling R-23), so a string would raise at parse time instead of firing the rule. The integer half of BP-008 is covered by tests/unit/test_models_accept_broken_documents.py.
BP-011 must NOT fire here: ruling R-18 gives it schema syntax with entity refs stripped, so an unresolvable entity is BP-009 alone.
assign_training's output_schema is referenced by no edge condition, so BP-010 has nothing to say about it.

The only case that swaps the resolver. BP-016 is not a property of the document - it is a property of the store, so it needs a resolver that reports location-onboarding 1.0.0 as already published (ruling R-11). The default blueprint resolver knows nothing published, which is the right answer for a first publish and for blueprint_validate.

mutate.value: Edited in place after publication, which BP-016 forbids.

cases.note: `replace`, never `remove`: `pool` is a required field, so removing it would raise at parse time rather than firing the rule.
Warning only (ruling R-13): the blueprint still publishes, so ok is true and the warning is present. BP-019's catalogue wording states the satisfied condition; the finding is the absence of notes.
When the blueprint cannot be resolved, every rule that needs it is skipped - there is nothing to check a fixture against. The document-local rules still run and this document passes them all.

Ruling R-07's second amendment: `output` is optional on NodeFixture, because R-07 blesses an absent output on a faulted fixture - so DS-004 owns presence. With no fault set, an absent output is this rule's finding rather than a parse-time exception.
DS-006 checks the entity_id segment only (ruling R-18); DS-009 owns @revision.
Warning only: an entity nothing references is dead weight in the world, but it blocks nothing.

Ruling R-14 fixed the shipped case: its first operation replaced a value with itself. `franchisee` declares no revisions, so its embedded state in receive_request must match entities.franchisee.base, where existing_locations is 1. DS-008 locates embedded state at each site the node's schema marks with an entity ref - see DECISIONS.md.
DS-010 is skipped when DS-009 has fired on the same reference (ruling R-02), so this reports one id.
after_docs comes into being after request_docs runs, and no path leads from request_docs to fetch_store_profile, so that fixture cannot show the revised state.
DS-010 is skipped when after_node names no node: DS-011 owns that.
DS-004 must NOT fire here: ruling R-18 gives every pool fixture to DS-019, and DS-004/DS-005 cover `nodes` only.

Ruling R-28: before it, a pool entry's `input` was validated by nothing - R-18 gives pools to DS-019, whose text named only `output_schema`, and DS-005 covers `nodes` only. request_docs takes a `doc_type` string.

The pool half of ruling R-07's second amendment. `output` became optional on NodeFixture, which every pool entry also uses, so DS-019 has to own presence for pools exactly as DS-004 does for nodes - otherwise a pool entry with no output and no fault validates clean, parses clean, and fetch_step serves a fixture with nothing in it.

Ruling R-23 asks for a real corpus case here rather than a coverage exemption. `seed` is StrictInt on the model, so this document does not parse - and it does not need to: the validator runs against the raw dict before any model is constructed, which is the whole point of validating the submitted document.
`replace`, never `remove`: `narrative` is required on the model, so the presence half is structural and only the content half is a rule.

Two findings, both DS-022: an unknown `kind` and an undeclared key. FaultSpec is extra=allow on the model on purpose (ruling R-07), so the unknown key reaches this rule instead of raising. DS-004 is skipped entirely because `fault` is set.
warning only, the dataset still stores
Warning only. intent says why the dataset exists in the suite; rationale says why this outcome is right in this world. Contracts 2.2: both are required, neither substitutes for the other.
DS-033 is the one rule the ruling register adds (R-21), mirroring DS-026 so that `rationale: ""` can no longer validate clean.
Proves the validator reports every problem in one pass rather than stopping at the first. A validator returning only the first error passes a membership check and fails this one.
proves errors from three different validators surface in one pass

Ruling R-07's other half, and the fault fixture it asks the corpus to carry: when `fault` is set, DS-004 skips output_schema validation entirely and requires only that `output` be absent or an object. This output would violate verify_compliance's output_schema outright, and the document must still validate clean.

The other direction of ruling R-07's second amendment, and the composite M2's review found: this document must validate clean AND parse. Before the amendment it did the first and not the second - zero findings, then `('nodes','verify_compliance','output') missing` from Dataset.model_validate, which is an exception where a rule id belongs.

raw_text_cases.note: The one rule no JSON Patch can reach: duplicate object keys collapse at parse time, and a dict cannot hold one key twice. Ruling R-20 keeps the rule and detects it at the tool boundary, where the raw text still exists, so this case is a text substitution rather than a mutation. The surviving value is a legal persona, so DS-012 stays silent and the expected set is exactly DS-013.
